task: settle 0x0177caa8 in ONE run: initial bytes, READ+WRITE watch, every write path
answer: The 1 at 0x0177caa8 is written by an stw inside f_0091f364, reached by the call at 0x00609a3c from f_006099e8 (guest lr 0x00609a40), one instruction after it stores 0 to the same word. It precedes every read of 1 by 0.18-1.13 s across four runs. The word is zero-fill BSS: PT_LOAD[1] segment offset 0x44caa8, beyond filesz 0x1bc014, so the ELF holds no initial value, and the arm-time read before the first guest instruction logged 0x00000000.

evidence.run_E: 1956 guest events, 0 self reads, 576 events on the word, 0 chain gaps; 0->1 at 2.393590 (lr 0x00609a40), first read==1 at 2.840156 (lr 0x0091fdb0), 0 reads==1 before the write
evidence.write_named: stw r10,0(r11) at 0x0091f3d4 in f_0091f364; r11 = [TOC-32220] = 0x0177caa8, r10 = 1 on the counter-is-zero arm
evidence.instruments_agree: mprotect READ+WRITE trap and software block watch (rsv::store_range) report the same six writes in the same order from the same guest lr
evidence.watcher_defect_found_and_fixed: the block watch's own vm::read32 of a trap page was published as a guest READ carrying the interrupted store's lr; 6 of 575 events in the unfixed run. Fixed with a thread_local self-read depth, counted and printed.
